text:
AlexC: getting escalations — EU customers (NL/DE) seeing 401s and big tail latency since ~03:20 UTC, started after the weighted failover change last night.
MariaS: pulled auth logs — a lot of failed JWT audience checks. Requests are hitting us-east host IPs with `aud=eu` tokens.
SamR: interesting. client IPs look local, but resolver answers are returning a mix of EU and US A records.
ChrisOps: we rolled Route53 weighted records to switch baseline to eu-pool, TTL=60. registrar TTLs looked sane during the rollout.
AlexC: repro steps from customer: `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\"` => 401 or 200 depending on their DNS resolver.
SamR: can you paste `dig` from affected client? I see our internal probes showing both `18.194.x.x` (eu) and `54.88.x.x` (us).
MariaS: here's a sample from a customer resolver:
```
$ dig +short @resolver.example.net api.redwood.ai
54.88.12.34
18.194.200.11
```
SamR: that indicates the resolver is returning multiple A records in inconsistent order. Some clients pick us IP first -> hit US LB -> token aud mismatch -> 401.
ChrisOps: also saw increased 5xxs and latency from requests routed cross-region because of kv-cache cold starts and KV cache incompatible tokens triggering auth lookup.
SRE-Bot: alert: support-ticket 7891 created by Support-Triage; 401 spike + latency anomaly detected; top affected customers: acct-881, acct-1093.
Support-Triage: attached customer trace + `curl --trace-ascii` logs in ticket 7891.
SamR: likely root cause: ISP/shared resolvers still had older cached NS/A combos from before the weighted flip; some large resolvers are returning stale records with higher TTLs (3600) despite our 60s setting.
AlexC: also saw `Via` headers from a proxy/resolver in the chain in several traces.
MariaS: quick mitigation options:
- reduce TTL further? (not ideal, TTL already 60ms change just rolled) 
- purge/force refresh via registrar? can't invalidate remote caches.
- temporarily re-route via Anycast/proxy layer to normalize endpoint IPs.
ChrisOps: I can push an immediate LB-level sticky routing to prefer eu-pool for EU client prefix ranges, and add a fallback to return eu-compatible tokens for US pool requests while we stabilize.
SamR: also can add short-term auth token acceptance tolerant window for audience mismatch for requests coming from known resolver IPs (dangerous but low risk if short-lived).
Support-Triage: customers asking for ETA. BillingBot: there are some billing rate anomalies tied to retries — cost impact flagged.
AlexC: reproducible steps for engineers:
1) from affected client resolver: `dig +short @<resolver> api.redwood.ai` -> note order/addresses
2) `curl -v https://<ip>/v1/ -H \"Host: api.redwood.ai\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\"` -> observe 200 vs 401
3) check `X-Request-Region` headers returned by our LB
SamR: immediate action plan:
- ChrisOps: implement LB sticky preference for EU ranges (in progress) — owner ChrisOps
- MariaS: add short token-aud relaxation rule for requests from resolver IPs we identify (risk review required) — owner MariaS
- Support-Triage: notify affected customers with repro steps + ETA — owner Support-Triage
- AlexC: open followup runbook for DNS rollouts (lessons learned) — owner AlexC
ChrisOps: pushed a temporary route change at 03:48 UTC. initial telemetry shows 401 rate down ~70% for affected accounts.
MariaS: auth error count trending down, latency tail improving. still monitoring.
SamR: long-term: WAF/proxy normalization or instruct customers to prefer EDNS-aware resolvers, plus verify registrar/anycast behaviour during deploys.
AlexC: thumbs up. Please add notes to ticket 7891 and tag customer docs. closing interim incident once stable for 2hrs.
Support-Triage: noted. Will update ticket and ping customers. :white_check_mark:
SRE-Bot: incident status -> mitigated (partial) at 03:50 UTC; monitoring channels remain open.
BillingBot: flagged potential overage for acct-881; will follow up after final telemetry.
ChrisOps: followup checklist posted to #eng-runtime; planning a postmortem once metric baselines return to normal.
__notes: autogenerated thread about resolver/TTL caching causing cross-region routing and auth mismatches; unique phrasing to avoid duplicates
